clue.text: Loves to go round 6 in which social workers leave kids?

definitions.text: in which social workers leave kids?

indicators.note: the term for loves goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: honeys are loved ones, darlings
the answer to 6 Down is RAKE, and to rake is to comb

explanation.surface: A cryptic tease about a place where social workers abandon children, built around a cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: The social workers are bees, a social insect, and the kids are their larvae, left in the wax cells.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees lay eggs in the hexagonal wax cells of their hives, so these structures hold the young of the colony.

clue.text: Signal not to go after a woman, one who wasn't ready?

indicators.note: the signal comes after the woman, so it is placed second

parts.note: Ethel is a woman's name
a red light tells traffic to stop

explanation.surface: A traffic light holds back a woman who was not prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: The English king nicknamed 'the Unready' was Ethelred II, so 'wasn't ready' is a playful paraphrase of his epithet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglo-Saxon king Ethelred II is known by the byname 'the Unready', meaning poorly advised.

clue.text: Soon about to embrace vice, outwardly displaying devotion

indicators.note: the reversed word for soon wraps round the outer letters of vice
about signals turning the word for soon backwards

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

indicators.note: outwardly keeps only the outside letters of the word vice

explanation.surface: Someone is soon to take up a vice while putting on a show of piety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the old word for soon, and 'outwardly' keeps the two outer letters of vice. 'displaying' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic practice this is a devotion of prayers said over nine successive days.

clue.text: Attention — quiet needed by Polish listening device

indicators.note: the earlier pieces come before the polish word, which follows them

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to give attention
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
to hone is to polish or sharpen

explanation.surface: An instruction that attention and quiet are what a Polish speaker needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with its capital pretends to be the nationality but is the verb polish.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small speaker worn at the ear for hearing audio, so a device for listening.

clue.text: Queen's accommodation in Taipei, fairly regularly visited

indicators.note: only every other letter of the two words is called on, at a steady interval

explanation.surface: A royal's lodgings in Taiwan's capital get a fair number of visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the even letters of TAIPEI FAIRLY. The queen is a queen bee, not a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where beehives are kept houses the colonies, each with its queen bee.

clue.text: Uncover a bit of northern Greek architecture

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so backwards
a bit of means a few letters are taken from inside the phrase

explanation.surface: An invitation to expose some of the architecture of northern Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of' takes EKAR from greEK ARchitecture, and 'northern' reads it upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To rake up, or rake over, the past is to uncover or dig out old matters.

clue.text: Working space satellite capturing salt lake, as an example

indicators.note: working and the moon together hold the sailor word between them

parts.note: on means operating, working
Io is one of the moons of Jupiter
a salt, like a tar, is an old sailor

explanation.surface: A satellite in orbit spots a salt lake while operating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt lake' looks like one phrase, but salt is the sailor and lake belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of North America's Great Lakes, so it is an example of a lake.

clue.text: Proportion of speech discovered?

indicators.note: dis-covered: the word for speech loses its cover, its first and last letters

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A question about how much of a speech was found out.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'discovered' as 'dis-covered', with the outer letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the relative size of two quantities, which is a proportion.

clue.text: General, Italian American, one who holds broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means the words are given out loud and spelt by how they sound

parts.note: a gripper is something or someone that holds

explanation.surface: A list: an army general, an Italian-American, and someone holding a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian American' reads as one phrase, but Italian ends the definition and American gives A.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Agrippa was a Roman commander, Augustus's right-hand man, so a general from Italy.

clue.text: Somehow limit a time when filling in summary

indicators.note: the short pieces fill the gap inside the word for summary

parts.note: a recap is a summary

explanation.surface: A way to restrict something by squeezing time into a summary.
explanation.walkthrough: AT goes after the first letter of RECAP. The first word looks like an anagram signal, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate-cap is to restrict, by law, the local tax a British council may levy: a particular way of limiting.

clue.text: Turn out fine, ultimately about to go into black

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word fine
the abbreviation for about goes inside the word for black

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black
c, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Things work out well in the end, about to plunge into the black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn out fine' reads as one phrase, but fine is the start of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn someone out is to throw them out, expel them by force.

clue.text: Elaborate exile having run away

indicators.note: the letter for run is taken away from the exile word

parts.note: an expatriate is someone living outside their homeland, an exile
r is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A detailed account of an exile who has fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run away' reads as fleeing, but run is R and away removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To expatiate is to speak or write at length, which is to elaborate on a topic.

clue.text: Initially, chef's assistant on board cooked stew

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the two words
cooked means the letters are prepared afresh, mixed up

explanation.surface: A chef's helper on board a ship prepared a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship's galley, but both words are the anagram's fodder, signalled by 'cooked'.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbonado is a dish of meat, scored and grilled or braised, listed in dictionaries as a stew.

clue.text: Lines contributing to hollow praise

indicators.note: the railway letters go into the hollow word, adding to it

parts.note: a cup is a hollow, as in a cup of the hands
RY, railway, means lines

explanation.surface: Lines that help make praise sound empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow praise' reads as empty flattery, but hollow is CUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry something up is to extol it or speak highly of it.

clue.text: Composed repeats in D flat?

indicators.note: composed means the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A musical question: was something written with repetitions in the key of D flat?
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface makes 'D flat' look like a key, but flat is the definition and D is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian writing or performance is dull and uninspired: flat.

clue.text: Some time in the past, padre blessed breadbasket

parts.note: the Middle Ages are a historical period

indicators.note: blessed suggests something worked over, so the padre's letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Long ago, a priest blessed a basket of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blessed' rearranges PADRE to PREAD. Breadbasket is slang for the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadbasket is slang for the belly, and this phrase means the paunch many people develop in their forties and fifties.

clue.text: Light, flavourless, plucked bird

indicators.note: plucked means stripped of the outside, so the edge letters go

parts.note: bland food lacks flavour
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A light dish: a tasteless, plucked bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plucked bird' suggests a carcass, but plucked trims BLAND to LAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp in a case, a light.

clue.text: Supplement programme with part of game nine

parts.note: an app is a software programme
an end is a division of play in bowls or curling
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Adding a programme with part of a game for nine players.
explanation.walkthrough: In bowls and curling, an end is one stage of a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A section of extra material added at the back of a book is a supplement to it.

clue.text: Foreign appearance

definitions.meaning: foreign in the sense of coming from outside, external
the outward look of someone or something

explanation.surface: An exotic look.
explanation.definitionFit: Exterior means outer or from outside, and also the outside surface one presents, an outward look.

clue.text: Offence involving small-time singer-songwriter, one of 12?

indicators.note: the word for offence wraps round the short time

parts.note: a sin is a moral offence
a mo is a moment, a small time

explanation.surface: A minor musician gets mixed up in a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small-time' looks like a slight on the singer, but it is MO, a moment. Paul Simon is the singer; Simon Peter was one of the twelve apostles.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Simon is a famous musician, and two of Jesus's twelve apostles bore the name.

clue.text: Stone workers present during roll call?

indicators.note: at a roll call names are read out and answered aloud, so the words are taken by sound

parts.note: men are workers, and here is what someone present answers

explanation.surface: Stonemasons who are present answering a register.
explanation.walkthrough: When the register is called, those present say 'here'.
explanation.definitionFit: A menhir is a tall upright prehistoric standing stone.

clue.text: Blithe Spirit only half reviewed, causing complaint

indicators.note: re-viewed, seen again in a new arrangement, so the letters are mixed
only the first half of the word Spirit is kept

explanation.surface: A critic gave Noel Coward's play Blithe Spirit only half a review, prompting a grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half' keeps SPI from Spirit, and 'reviewed' rearranges it with BLITHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlebitis, inflammation of a vein, is a medical complaint, an ailment.

clue.text: Where some go mainly to introduce daughter and dashing chap

indicators.note: the letter for daughter is introduced inside the shortened word
mainly means most of the word, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the ladies is a women's lavatory, where some people go

explanation.surface: A spot where some go to meet a girl's charming young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' trims LADIES to LADIE before D goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Laddie is a Scottish word for a boy or young man, a lively young fellow.

clue.text: Resist old Irishman

parts.note: to buck a trend is to resist it

explanation.surface: An aged son of Ireland putting up resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucko is an Irish form of address for a young man or lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucko is chiefly Irish slang for a young fellow, a lad, so it can mean an Irish chap.

clue.text: Business errand, extremely involved

parts.note: a concern is a business firm

indicators.note: extremely points to the two letters at the extremes of errand

explanation.surface: A company's errand turns out to be highly complicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely involved' reads as very complicated, but extremely takes ED from errand.
explanation.definitionFit: Being concerned in a matter means taking part in it, being implicated.

clue.text: Without having left, face familiar bloke

indicators.note: without having means the letter for left is taken out

parts.note: a clock face; to clock is also slang for face

explanation.surface: Confronting a well-known man once he has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: In London slang, 'cock' is a friendly term for a man, as in 'wotcha, cock'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cock is British slang for a mate, a friend, a matey way to address a man.

clue.text: European sacked in job tender

indicators.note: the European letter is sacked, thrown out of the word

parts.note: a career is a person's line of work

explanation.surface: A worker from the EU lost their job while tendering for work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' looks like a bid or adjective but is the noun: one who tends.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer looks after the sick or elderly, someone who tends them.

clue.text: EU character not for making EU wine

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, and Greece is in the EU
anti means against, not for

explanation.surface: A figure who opposes the EU fails to produce European wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red from Tuscany, in Italy, so a wine made within the EU.

clue.text: Woodlice poo said to be awful

indicators.note: something awful is in a bad state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A remark that woodlouse droppings are reportedly unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' looks like a homophone signal, but it is part of what gets rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Isopoda is the order of crustaceans to which woodlice belong.
